Subfactors, index and finite-depth classification

A generating tunnel and the classification theorem

The finite-index tunnel constructed in the preceding lesson need not yet generate the ambient factor. Its finite basis supplies the missing argument. A vector missed by every late rotation would remain orthogonal after multiplication on either side by the late factor. The same basis then makes it orthogonal to every vector, which is impossible. Both whole model pairs are invariant under every nonzero physical corner and positive real amplification, with their original and recovered traces kept separate. Exact corner maps preserve the full marked ladder and all canonical opposite cup and trace data. The marked upward invariant also determines the actual downward trace at every finite stage and reconstructs the whole ordinary standard model. This gives classification of proper strongly amenable separable inclusions without finite depth or extremality, while retaining the separate physical opposite-model trace. An ordinary core has its own complete tracial Jones tunnel. When its two endpoints are factors this tunnel is generating, which proves the original standard-model converse and the full proper/separable equivalence with strong amenability. At extremality the independent normal ordinary/opposite comparison proves both directions of the full physical opposite-model characterization, retaining both multiplication reversals and whole-pair endpoints.

We assume Matrix corners approximate a tunnel, Detecting a generating tunnel, and Reflected traces and a uniform bound along a tunnel. For the tracial ultraproduct we use Definition 3.1 and Theorems 3.2–3.3 of Ultraproducts and the asymptotic centralizer. They give a finite von Neumann algebra with faithful normal trace, and a factor when every coordinate algebra is a factor. Only that finite tracial specialization is needed. The bounded-vector arguments below are proved here. References are [Popa], [Jones] and [McDuff].

The standard invariant determines the inclusion

Theorem 17.6 — finite-depth classification. Two finite-index, finite-depth inclusions of separable hyperfinite II₁ factors are isomorphic as inclusions if and only if their structured standard invariants are isomorphic, including their inclusions, normalized traces and Jones projections.

Proof. An inclusion isomorphism extends up the Jones tower and gives the invariant isomorphism, by Proposition 12.1.

Conversely, first suppose the common index is greater than one. By Theorem 17.5 choose generating tunnels for both inclusions. Corollary 14.5 supplies trace-preserving anti-isomorphisms to their reflected pairs

The invariant isomorphism maps each and to its counterpart, preserves the compatible traces and maps to . Its isometry on the tracial completion of the union extends normally to its von Neumann closure. This extension restricts to an isomorphism of the closures and carries their subalgebras commuting with these projections to one another. Equation (14.9) therefore makes it an isomorphism of the pairs in (17.14). Using the ambient ladder matters here: does not generally belong to .

Compose with the anti-isomorphism from the first generating tunnel and the inverse anti-isomorphism from the second. Products are reversed twice, giving an ordinary normal isomorphism carrying onto .

At index one, the inclusion is the identity inclusion by the dimension theorem. The separable hyperfinite II₁ factor is unique up to isomorphism, so the identity inclusions are isomorphic. Their Jones tunnels are constant and do not satisfy the proper-inclusion generating-tunnel assertion; this endpoint is handled directly. The index itself is part of the invariant, since . This also separates the identity case from the proper case.

The invariant used in the theorem is the structured ladder of finite-dimensional algebras. A principal graph records dimensions and multiplicities; it need not determine the ladder's embeddings and commuting-square data. Graph realization and the number of inclusions for a given graph require further arguments.

Classification without finite depth or extremality

Theorem 17.10 — arbitrary-depth strongly amenable classification. Let and be finite-index II₁ inclusions with separable preduals. Assume each satisfies the original all-smooth representation amenability and has ergodic actual ordinary core, exactly as in SA.1. Then they are isomorphic as inclusions if and only if their structured standard invariants 12.2 are isomorphic, with their inclusions, normalized tower traces and marked Jones projections. Neither extremality nor finite depth is required.

Proof. An inclusion isomorphism preserves the normalized factor trace and extends up the actual towers with their cups, by 12.1, giving the forward implication. For the converse, SA.7 supplies an actual generating ordinary tunnel for each inclusion, at the stated hypotheses and with any prescribed finite prefix retained. The corresponding ordinary core pairs are literally the two original pairs. Theorem 17.9, applied to the given invariant isomorphism, compares those whole core pairs normally and trace preservingly. Its range therefore gives an isomorphism carrying onto . Equivalently one may use any two old cores and compose(17.27) with the already supplied standard-part maps of SA.7. This proves the classification without an opposite-model normality assumption.

At index one the structured invariant and ordinary core are scalar. Within the separable hyperfinite class of 17.6 the identity inclusions are isomorphic by the existing factor-uniqueness theorem, as proved there. No classification of arbitrary identity inclusions by their scalar invariant is asserted. Properness in 17.10 keeps this endpoint distinct; it is also the proper-inclusion scope of the generating theorem SA.7.

A core carries its own ordinary tunnel

The standard model is defined as the whole inherited-trace core pair, rather than a copy of part of that pair inside some larger representation. We now prove that a factorial ordinary core has an actual generating tunnel inside itself. This supplies the full standard-model converse in Popa, Theorem 4.1.2(v) and Theorem 5.1.1, printed pp.210 and 226, without using a physical opposite-model identification.

We retain the ordinary tunnel notation of 51.1:

Throughout this section the original inclusion is proper, with finite index , and . The original ambient factors need not have separable predual. Lemma 51.1 already proves that the normal tracial expectations restrict to , that , that , and that . We use those results without repeating their density proof. The full bounded bases come from 52.1, applied at each shifted ordinary inclusion.

The top row is the actual intersection tower inside the original larger core. Each original cup implements its entire internal basic construction, including the displayed partial Gram corner and canonical trace (17.14). When both starting core algebras are factors, the internal commutants generate the whole core (17.15). Transport through a whole-pair isomorphism gives the original standard-model converse (17.16). The lower comparison retains the two normal anti-isomorphisms and their identical physical opposite endpoints at extremality; their composition is the whole ordinary-model isomorphism (17.52–17.53). The original standard-model converse

Theorem 17.16. Let be a finite-index inclusion of II₁ factors with separable predual. The following are equivalent:

  1. Original strong amenability.
  2. Global finite approximation(G) of 61.56.
  3. Existence of an ordinary generating tunnel.
  4. Existence of a generating continuation after every prescribed finite ordinary prefix.
  5. A normal isomorphism of the whole pair onto its ordinary standard model , for one, equivalently every, choice of the defining ordinary tunnel.
